The original localhost:4000 paper body was unreachable at reconstruction time, so this is rebuilt from those sources and the built code — not a byte-copy of the lost original. Canonical ledger: the hyperquiz-epic task tree on guerrilla.

The realtime layer is server-authoritative. The Room GenServer owns game state; clients send intent (a choice, a pointer position) and receive rendered frames. No client is trusted with scoring or timing.

items.value: Socket /quiz — anonymous, carrying a signed player token minted on join (reconnect identity survives a dropped socket, P6).
Channel quiz:room:<pin> — one per running game, joined by PIN.
quiz:events:<pin> — authoritative state (phase changes, question pushes, tallies).
quiz:cursors:<pin> — individual cursor frames (below the crossover threshold).
quiz:heat:<pin> — the aggregate heatmap frame (above the threshold).

blocks.content: Players stream continuous pointer/touch position at ~30Hz (quiz-cursors.js pointermove, throttled to 33ms) — NOT a tap-hold or drag-a-dot gesture (this corrects the original input-decision text; see the decisions paper). The server treats a cursor as opaque normalized coordinates.

The Room batches cursor frames at 15Hz into a compact binary codec (Quiz.CursorFrame) and fans them out on quiz:cursors:<pin>. Batching + binary encoding keeps the per-tick payload bounded even with hundreds of concurrent pointers.

Above the crossover threshold the Room stops fanning out individual cursors and instead emits a fixed 32x32 heatmap — a constant 2,048-byte payload on quiz:heat:<pin>, independent of the number of players. See the scaling paper.

A Studio edit publishes the quiz content; Quiz.Bridge picks up the change and calls Room.apply_question on the running room, which pushes new state on quiz:events:<pin>. Every host and player screen re-renders with no reload, in under a second.
